title: Template API Reference
content: Template API Reference Every .marko file exposes its runtime API on its default export. Targeted compilation emits render in server builds and mount in browser builds.

title: Template.render(input)
content:
Parameter Default Details input {} Template input object; may also include $global for render-scoped globals Available in server builds. Returns a render result that can be consumed as a stream, async iterable, ReadableStream, promise, or synchronous string. [!WARNING]
A render result can only be consumed once; later consumers fail (thrown, rejected, or emitted as a stream error). Awaiting the same result multiple times is the sole exception because the first await caches its promise.

title: Async Iterator
content: The render result implements the async iterable protocol for for await...of, yielding HTML string chunks: Each iteration yields HTML flushed since the previous pull; synchronous renders yield a single chunk. Exiting the loop early (break, return, or throw) aborts any pending render, and calling iterator.throw(reason) aborts with reason.

title: Pipe
content: .pipe(target) streams rendered HTML into a Node.js stream.Writable (or any object implementing write(chunk) and end()). If target.flush() exists, it is called after each chunk so buffering transforms such as zlib.createGzip() flush incrementally:

title: ReadableStream
content: .toReadable() returns a WHATWG ReadableStream<Uint8Array> yielding UTF-8 encoded chunks, suitable for Web APIs such as Response and edge runtimes: Consumption starts on the stream's first pull, so an unread Response leaves the render unconsumed. Cancelling the stream aborts the render with the cancellation reason.

title: Thenable
content:
The render result is a thenable whose resolved value is the full buffered HTML string, supporting await, .then(), .catch(), and .finally(): [!NOTE]
Awaiting buffers the full HTML document into a single string rather than streaming chunks.

title: toString
content:
.toString() returns the rendered HTML synchronously when the template has no asynchronous content: [!CAUTION]
Any asynchronous rendering (such as <await>) or an already aborted $global.signal causes .toString() to throw rather than return partial HTML.

title: Template.mount(input, node, position?)
content:
Parameter Default Details input {} Template input object; may also include $global node (required) Light DOM Element where the template is inserted position "beforeend" Insertion point relative to node, matching Element.insertAdjacentHTML Available in browser builds. Builds the reactive DOM and inserts it relative to node: node must be a light DOM Element (not a ShadowRoot or DocumentFragment): Marko inherits the element's HTML namespace during parsing and delegates events on document. [!NOTE]
Supported position values match insertAdjacentHTML():

title: Mounted Instance
content:
Template.mount() returns a mounted instance with methods to update or destroy the template and read its return value: [!WARNING]
Use instance.update() and instance.destroy() only at client-only mount boundaries or in tests. Within Marko templates, manage updates through the reactive system. instance.update(input) Applies new input synchronously as a reactive update. $global is fixed at mount time and ignored on updates: instance.destroy() Removes the template's DOM nodes, aborts every $signal, and runs cleanup hooks: instance.value Reflects the tag variable exposed by the template's <return>:

title: input.$global
content: A $global property passed in input to render or mount is stripped from input and exposed as $global across every template in the render tree. Application-specific globals sit alongside Marko's built-in properties and are typed on Marko.Global.

title: $global.serializedGlobals
content:
string[] | Record<string, boolean> | undefined $global stays server-only by default. Properties listed in serializedGlobals are also serialized into the HTML so browser code can read them on $global: An object form suits lists assembled across middleware, matching Marko Run's ctx.serializedGlobals: Properties holding undefined are omitted. [!WARNING]
Serialized values are embedded in the HTML response and visible to clients. Keep secrets off serializedGlobals.

title: $global.signal
content: AbortSignal | undefined Aborts pending async rendering and cleans up active work when signaled, such as when an incoming HTTP request disconnects.

title: $global.cspNonce
content: string | undefined Adds a nonce attribute to Marko-rendered <script> and <style> elements: <html-script> and <html-style>, dynamic <style> elements, and inline streaming/resume scripts. An explicit nonce attribute (or spread) on an element takes precedence. Marko automatically serializes cspNonce to the client whenever it is set on $global, so it does not need to be listed in serializedGlobals.

title: $global.renderId
content:
string | undefined Isolates multiple independent renders sharing one runtime in the same document. Defaults to "_", except for non-page templates (whose rendered tag tree contains no html, head, or body element) compiled with linkAssets, which receive a fresh random ID per render() call. mount() always defaults to "_". Set an explicit renderId when multiple renders of page templates share a document: [!WARNING]
renderId and runtimeId become JavaScript identifiers in inline resume scripts and must match /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/ (no UUIDs or hyphens).

title: $global.runtimeId
content: string | undefined Names the global variable holding resume data for a Marko runtime instance (default "M"), isolating multiple Marko runtimes on the same page. Follows the same identifier rule as renderId. Server and browser builds must match, so configure runtimeId in the bundler (for example @marko/vite's runtimeId option) rather than per render call.

title: Supported Environments
content: Supported Environments Marko targets modern browsers and maintained Node.js releases across both its compiler and runtime packages.

title: Browser
content: Marko supports the browsers covered by eBay's browserslist-config. @marko/compiler also respects a project's own browserslist configuration when generating browser output. <browser-support></browser-support>

title: Node.js
content: Marko packages require Node.js >=22.12.0, tracking actively maintained releases on the official Node.js release schedule.

title: Reactivity Reference
content: Reactivity Reference Marko's reactivity system tracks dependencies between state and DOM output at compile time, updating only the affected nodes when values change. Mutable state starts with <let>.

title: Reactive Variables
content: Tag variables, tag parameters, and input are reactive. Writable state comes from <let> and assignable <return> tags; other tag variables (<const>, <id>, <define>, element references) are derived or read-only. $global is not reactive.

title: Render Expressions
content:
Any expression in a template that reads a reactive variable re-evaluates when that variable changes. Reactive expressions appear in attributes, tag arguments, dynamic text, dynamic tag names, <style> dynamic values, <html-comment>, and <script> bodies. [!NOTE]
Module-level statements (import, export, static, server, and client) run once when the template module loads and are outside the reactive graph. Clicking the button reassigns count, and the button text updates automatically. [!CAUTION]
The compiler may group or reorder render expressions into shared update functions, so render expressions must be pure. [!TIP]
Marko resolves its reactive dependency graph at compile time rather than tracking subscriptions at runtime, generating direct DOM updates for each state variable.

title: Scheduling Updates
content: Marko compares updates by reference equality (===) and batches changes into an update queue flushed on the next microtask. Updates scheduled after the microtask flush but before the browser paints are deferred to the next animation frame. This ensures: Content ready to paint is not blocked Reactive feedback loops are throttled to at most one cycle per frame Updates in background tabs pause until the document is visible For visual motion, prefer CSS Animations, CSS Transitions, or the Web Animations API.

title: Stale Derived Values
content:
Assigning to an uncontrolled <let> writes the new value into scope immediately, so subsequent lines in the same handler read the updated value. (A controllable <let> invokes its valueChange handler instead, updating only when the owner updates and flushes.) Derived values such as <const> and rendered DOM nodes recompute when the queue flushes, so they still hold the previous state for the rest of the handler: [!WARNING]
Reading subtotal or the DOM inside the handler after quantity++ returns the value from the previous render because the update queue has not flushed yet.

title: Native Tags
content: Native Tags Native tags are built-in HTML, SVG, and MathML elements. In Marko they follow standard HTML semantics with targeted ergonomic enhancements. Attributes on native tags (including custom elements registered with "html": true) are written via setAttribute, except for Marko's built-in controllable bindings. To assign JavaScript properties directly on a custom element, use an element reference inside <script>.

title: Element References
content:
Every native tag exposes a tag variable returning a getter for its DOM node: [!CAUTION]
DOM nodes exist only in the browser, and element getters are readable only in post-render code: <script> bodies, <lifecycle> hooks, and event handlers. Attributes, <const>, and interpolations evaluate during render.

title: class=
content: Accepts strings, objects, and arbitrarily nested arrays: All three render the same HTML: Object keys are class names included when their value is truthy (one level deep, never recursively traversed). Array entries may nest and spread, skipping falsy entries. Each class name may appear only once across a class= value (except across mutually exclusive ternary branches), because Marko updates individual toggled classes independently.

title: style=
content:
Accepts strings, objects, and arbitrarily nested arrays: All three render display:block;margin-right:16px (joined with ;, no trailing ;). Object keys write verbatim as hyphen-case CSS property names. [!WARNING]
Unlike the DOM style API, keys are not converted from camelCase: Values stringify verbatim with no unit inference ({ "margin-right": 16 } renders margin-right:16, not 16px). Use numbers only for unitless properties (line-height, z-index) or 0. A declaration is dropped when its value is false, null, undefined, "", NaN, or 0n, matching skipped dynamic text values. 0 is kept ({ width: 0 } renders width:0). [!TIP]
TypeScript rejects false as a style object property value, so place conditional declarations inside an array: Arrays nest and spread as in class=, and each CSS property may appear only once in a style= value. Custom properties (--foo) write verbatim and can be typed via Marko.CSS.Properties.

title: content=
content: Native elements that accept child markup accept body content via content=. The value may be a variable, an imported template, an attribute tag carrying content, a falsy value, or the surrounding template's input.content. Because content is part of input, a spread forwards both attributes and children: Pass content= explicitly to target an inner wrapper element: content= is reactive; swapping the value replaces the inner content without recreating the host element: [!WARNING] Any literal tag body takes precedence over content=, including a body containing only a comment: Attributes merge left to right: placing content= after a spread overrides forwarded content, and content=undefined drops forwarded content while keeping all other attributes: Void elements (, , etc.) and raw-text elements (

title: Event Handlers
content:
Attributes beginning with on followed by - or a capital letter register event listeners. on- preserves exact event casing, while onCamelCase lowercases the event name (in TypeScript, standard DOM events use exact camelCase spellings such as onKeyDown): onDblClick → dblclick on-DblClick → DblClick Values must be a function or a falsy value, enabling conditional listeners: [!TIP]
Use on- for custom elements that dispatch mixed-case event names. [!CAUTION]
Avoid native inline HTML string handlers; they bypass Marko reactivity and conflict with strict CSP policies: Handler Arguments Every event handler receives (event, target): the Event and the element carrying the on* attribute: Unlike event.target (which may be a clicked descendant element), the second parameter is always the element with the handler attached. Because handlers are delegated on document, use the second argument or an element reference rather than event.currentTarget. Delegation Marko attaches a single capture-phase listener per event type on document and dispatches matching handlers from the event target upward through bubbling ancestors: Marko handlers run before listeners attached with addEventListener on the element or any descendant of document. Calling event.stopPropagation() inside a Marko handler stops ancestor Marko handlers as well as addEventListener listeners below document (including on the same element). Calling it in an addEventListener listener below document does not affect Marko handlers, which have already run. Non-bubbling events (focus, blur, load) invoke only the handler on the target element. Events inside a Shadow DOM retarget to the host before reaching document, so Marko's delegated handlers operate on light DOM trees.

title: Enhanced Value Attributes
content: Marko adds uniform state attributes to native form controls whose DOM state is normally split across child elements or properties. Radio and Checkbox <input type="radio"> and <input type="checkbox"> support checkedValue=, marking the input checked whenever checkedValue= matches value=: String checkedValue=: selects one matching radio input (keep name= for native form submission and keyboard navigation). String array checkedValue=: checks every checkbox whose value= is in the array. <select> <select> supports value= as a string (single select) or string array (<select multiple>), setting selected on matching <option> elements using string comparison (value=25 matches <option value="25">; null or undefined matches an empty value=). When <select> uses value= or valueChange=, every nested <option> (including inside <optgroup> or <for>) must declare its own value=, and initial selection comes from the <select> rather than selected= on <option>. <textarea> <textarea> accepts its value through either its body or value= (not both). Static <textarea> body text decodes HTML character references and re-escapes through the value path.

title: Change Handlers
content:
Native controls that maintain internal browser state (<input>, <select>, <textarea>, <details>, <dialog>) are uncontrolled by default: setting value= writes only the HTML default attribute while the browser owns edits. Adding a matching *Change attribute makes the control controlled by Marko state. Every user edit invokes the handler, and the DOM reflects the bound state: Use an explicit change handler to normalize, validate, or mask input before storing it: <input> Supports valueChange= (for editable input types), checkedChange=, and checkedValueChange=: [!CAUTION]
<input> always delivers string values. Convert numeric inputs in the handler or with a refining function: Checkbox checked= binding: Radio and multi-checkbox checkedValue= binding (a handler that ignores the new value keeps the current selection): <select> (valueChange=) Supports valueChange= for single strings or string arrays (multiple): <textarea> (valueChange=) Supports valueChange= paired with value=: <details> Supports openChange= paired with open=. Without openChange=, open= applies only on initial render: <dialog> Supports openChange= paired with open= for non-modal dialogs: [!WARNING]
openChange= observes the open attribute via MutationObserver and controls non-modal dialogs only. Calling .showModal() sets open and conflicts with a controlled openChange= binding. Manage modal dialogs directly with .showModal() and .close() without openChange=. Form Reset Resetting a form (<button type="reset"> or form.reset()) restores each controlled form element to its initial rendered value and invokes its change handler with that restored value so bound state stays synchronized: [!NOTE]
Reset change handlers run on the next animation frame. Calling preventDefault() on the reset event cancels both the reset and the handler calls.

title: Attribute Spreads
content:
A spread on a native tag owns the element's attribute set: attributes removed from the spread object are removed from the DOM on update: [!WARNING]
Attribute removal covers every attribute on the element, including attributes added outside Marko. Place attributes that must persist either inside the spread object or after the spread. Attributes written after a spread are excluded from the spread's ownership, letting wrapper tags pin or compose attributes while forwarding input: Attributes written before a spread merge into the spread object and are overridden by matching keys in the spread. class=, style=, and change handlers retain their special handling inside spreads. An event handler written after a spread claims that event so the spread does not attach a duplicate listener, while still exposing the original handler on input.

title: Enhanced Tags
content: Three HTML constructs have enhanced behavior in Marko, with raw fallbacks when literal HTML output is needed.

title: <script>
content: Marko's <script> runs reactive browser effects. Emit a literal HTML <script> element with <html-script>:

title: <style>
content: Marko's <style> extracts and bundles CSS. Emit a literal inline HTML <style> element with <html-style>.

title: <!-- comment -->
content: Marko strips comments by default. Emit a literal <!-- comment --> with <html-comment>.

title: Lazy Loading
content:
Lazy Loading By default, every custom tag used on a page is bundled into that page's JavaScript. Adding a load import attribute splits the tag into its own browser bundle, fetched only after a trigger fires. On the server, a lazily loaded tag renders its HTML immediately like any other tag; only its browser JavaScript is deferred until the trigger fires and the bundle arrives. In the browser, nothing renders in the tag's place until both the trigger and bundle resolve, and <try> can display placeholder content in the meantime. Attributes passed to a lazily loaded tag stay reactive while it loads, so the tag receives the latest values when its bundle arrives. [!NOTE]
The load attribute applies to default imports of custom tags (relative paths or tag import shorthand) declared before their first use. Lazily loaded tags render directly without tag variables.

title: Triggers
content:
The load value is a static string read at build time: either "render" alone, or one or more triggers joined with |. Trigger Selector Options Fires when render None None The tag renders (cannot combine with |) visible<selector> Required rootMargin=<css> The matched element enters the viewport idle None timeout=<ms> The browser becomes idle media<query> None None matchMedia(query) matches on<Event><sel> Required None The event first fires on the matched element Selectors match via document.querySelector: visible#hero, visible.hero, and visible[data-hero] attach directly, while a bare type selector needs a leading space (visible section). [!NOTE]
During SSR, the trigger script runs as the tag's HTML chunk flushes, so the watched element must already exist in the document. If a selector matches no element, the bundle loads immediately.

title: render
content: Splits the tag into its own bundle loaded as soon as the tag renders, useful for conditional or heavy components. Must be used alone (cannot combine with multiple triggers).

title: visible
content: Loads the bundle when the matched element enters the viewport via IntersectionObserver: Pass rootMargin in a query string to preload before the element enters the viewport:

title: idle
content: Loads the bundle when the browser is idle via requestIdleCallback (or immediately if unsupported). Accepts an optional timeout in milliseconds and no selector:

title: media
content:
Loads the bundle once matchMedia matches the given media query (immediately if already matched). Accepts both parenthesized media features (media(max-width: 768px)) and media types (media print): [!TIP]
Wrap a media-triggered tag in a facade to apply the trigger consistently at every call site.

title: Events
content: A trigger starting with on followed by - or a capital letter loads the bundle the first time that event fires on the matched element: Event casing follows native event handler rules: on- preserves casing, while onCamelCase lowercases the event name (on-click and onClick are equivalent).

title: Multiple Triggers
content: Join triggers with | to load as soon as the first one fires:

title: Facade Tags
content:
Because load applies per import site, wrapping a heavy tag in a facade makes it lazily loaded everywhere without repeating the trigger. [!WARNING]
All lazy import sites of the same tag share one bundle, so multiple imports of the same tag should declare the same trigger. A facade keeps the trigger in one place. Place the implementation inside a nested tags/ directory so only the facade can import it: Consumers use <location-map> directly with no load attribute, and the wrapper provides the selector target for visible.

title: Placeholders & Errors
content: In the browser, a lazily loaded tag integrates with <try> like <await>: @placeholder renders while waiting for the trigger and while the bundle fetches, and @catch handles load failures:

title: Bundler Support
content:
Lazy loading relies on the linkAssets compiler option, which @marko/vite and Marko Run configure automatically. [!NOTE]
Builds without linkAssets (such as @marko/vite with linked: false) cannot code-split; with { load } imports compile as eager imports and render normally.

title: Language Reference
content: Language Reference Marko is a superset of well-formed HTML. It enforces strict tag structure while extending HTML with JavaScript expressions, control flow, and compiled reactivity.

title: Syntax Legend
Template Variables
content: Three variables are automatically available inside every template body.

title: input
content: A JavaScript object holding the attributes passed to a custom tag, or the data passed to the Template API.

title: $signal
content:
An AbortSignal available inside template expressions, event handlers, and effect blocks (not in module-level statements). $signal exists only in the browser and is used to clean up side effects. It aborts when: Any reactive value (tag variable, tag parameter, or input) read by the expression or effect using $signal changes, including reads inside callbacks it registers The template or tag content is removed from the DOM [!CAUTION]
$signal is browser-only. Reading it during a server render (such as in an attribute, <const>, or interpolation) is invalid: Use $signal only in browser-only contexts: <script> bodies, <lifecycle> hooks, and event handlers. [!TIP]
Pass $signal directly to web APIs such as addEventListener() for automatic cleanup. To register a run-once listener whose callback reads reactive state without re-registering on every change, use <lifecycle>.

title: $global
content: Provides access to the render globals passed to the Template API.

title: Statements
content: Marko supports module-scoped statements at the root of a template. These run once when the template module loads rather than on every render.

title: import
content: Standard JavaScript import statements are valid at the template root and are shorthand for static import. Tag import Shorthand Angle brackets in the from specifier resolve a custom tag using Marko's tag discovery rules: Lazy Tag import Adding a load import attribute splits the tag into a separate browser bundle loaded on demand: See Lazy Loading for triggers and constraints.

title: export
content: Named JavaScript export statements are valid at the template root. The default export is reserved for the template itself.

title: static
content: Statements prefixed with static execute in module scope when the template loads on both server and browser. Any valid JavaScript statement, declaration, or block is supported (a static { ... } block unwraps its top-level bindings into module scope):

title: server and client
content: Statements prefixed with server or client execute in module scope only in that target environment. Bindings declared in one environment evaluate to undefined in the other. Environment prefixes also combine with import statements and blocks:

title: Tags
content:
Marko supports all native HTML, SVG, and MathML tags alongside core tags and custom tags (local or installed via node_modules). All tags share the same syntax: Any tag without content may be self-closed (
). Void elements such as and
require neither a closing tag nor a trailing /. Any closing tag may omit its name:

title: Attributes
content:
Attribute values are JavaScript expressions, including quoted strings (str="Hello" is a JavaScript string literal, not an HTML attribute string): Dynamic native attribute values are encoded for HTML attribute syntax (escaping the active quote character, \r, and & when it would begin a character reference). [!CAUTION]
Attribute encoding protects HTML syntax only. URL-valued attributes such as href and src are written as given, so check untrusted URLs against an allowlist of schemes (excluding javascript:, data:, and unexpected protocol-relative // URLs). [!CAUTION]
Unenclosed > is ambiguous with the end of a tag, so wrap comparisons with > in parentheses. Whitespace-preceded >= and arrow functions (=>) need no parentheses:

title: Skipped Attributes
content: Attributes whose value is null, undefined, or false are omitted from the HTML output. Other falsy values (0, 0n, NaN, and "") are still written, except empty class="" and style="", which are omitted. Dynamic text uses different skip rules.

title: Boolean Attributes
content:
A valueless attribute evaluates to true. On native tags, true emits the attribute name with no value: [!IMPORTANT]
ARIA enumerated attributes expect explicit string values ("true" / "false"), not HTML boolean attributes:

title: Spread Attributes
content: Spread syntax applies an object of attributes to a tag: Attributes merge from left to right, with later attributes overriding earlier ones. The spread target can be any JavaScript expression, including an object literal shorthand: On native tags, a spread also manages removal of attributes dropped on subsequent updates.

title: Shorthand Methods
content: Method definitions pass functions concisely as attributes: Native tag event handlers also receive the attached element as a second parameter. Prefix the method with async to use await inside its body:

title: Shorthand Change Handlers (Two-Way Binding)
content: attr:=x is optional shorthand for passing both attr= and attrChange=. Its right-hand side must be a tag variable, a destructured object property, or a property accessor (including optional input.a?.b and computed obj[key] access). For a mutable tag variable, := desugars to an assignment handler: For a property accessor (or a destructured object property such as <const/{ count }=input>), := forwards the corresponding *Change property: Refining Function Insert :fn:= to transform values before passing them to the change handler: For property accessors, the generated handler only runs when the upstream change handler is defined:

title: Shorthand class and id
content: Emmet-style #id and .class shorthands attach directly to a tag name. Omitting the tag name defaults to div, and shorthand classes merge with any class= attribute. Interpolations work inside shorthand id and class names:

title: Shorthand value
content: Omitting the attribute name at the start of a tag passes the value as value=: Combining this with method shorthand passes a value function:

title: Attribute Termination
content:
Attributes may be separated with commas, which is primarily used for multiline attributes in concise syntax: [!CAUTION]
Wrap JavaScript comma expressions in parentheses so the comma is not parsed as an attribute separator:

title: Tag Content
content: Markup inside a tag's body is passed to the tag as input.content. Custom tags render it with a dynamic tag: Native tags also accept content= as an attribute, so the wrapper above can be written <div class="card" content=input.content/>.

title: Dynamic Text
content:
Interpolate JavaScript expressions inside tag content with ${expression}, matching JavaScript template literals: Static text in markup is emitted verbatim (preserving HTML character references). Dynamic ${...} text escapes <, &, and \r to <, &, and  to prevent XSS. Skipped Values Interpolated null, undefined, false, "", NaN, and 0n render nothing. All other values convert via string concatenation (0 renders 0, true renders true, arrays join with commas). The same skip rules apply inside <html-script> and <html-style>. [!NOTE]
Skipped attributes only omit null, undefined, and false, writing NaN, "", and 0n. [!WARNING]
Plain objects stringify to [object Object]. Render promises with <await> rather than interpolating the promise directly. Unescaped Text Prefix an interpolation with ! ($!{...}) to emit raw, unescaped HTML generated and sanitized elsewhere: [!CAUTION]
Unescaped interpolations write directly into the document and expose the page to XSS if given untrusted input.

title: Whitespace
content:
Runs of whitespace in markup collapse to a single space. Any whitespace-only run that begins with a line break is removed completely, keeping source indentation out of the output. Both tags and ${...} placeholders act as boundaries for this rule. Renders: [!WARNING] A line break immediately between tags or ${...} placeholders produces no space (Total: followed by a newline and ${amount} renders Total:5, and ${a} followed by a newline and ${b} renders AB). Keep a space on the same line when separation is needed. Whitespace is preserved verbatim inside 
,

title: Attribute Tags
content:
Tags prefixed with @ pass named or repeated sections of content and attributes into the parent tag's input instead of rendering directly: <my-layout> receives: [!NOTE]
Control flow tags (<if> and <for>) pass nested attribute tags upward to their enclosing tag; see Conditional Attribute Tags.

title: Nested Attribute Tags
content: Attribute tags can nest inside other attribute tags, becoming properties on their parent attribute tag: Provides the following input:

title: Repeated Attribute Tags
content:
When an attribute tag appears multiple times with the same name, the property exposes the first instance directly and implements the iterable protocol over all instances: Use singular names for attribute tags (<@item>, iterated as input.item) even when repeated. [!TIP]
Spread a repeated attribute tag into an array when random access or .length is needed:

title: Conditional Attribute Tags
content:
<if> and <for> apply attribute tags dynamically to their enclosing tag: [!NOTE]
A control flow branch may contain attribute tags or default content, not both in the same branch.

title: Tag Variables
content: Tag variables expose reactive values from a tag into the template scope, written as / followed by an identifier or destructuring pattern. Custom tags expose values through <return>. Native tags expose a getter function returning the DOM element (native tag variables must be a single identifier, not a destructuring pattern):

title: Tag Var Scope
content:
Function-valued tag variables (including native element references) are hoisted across the template body (excluding module statements). Non-function <let>, <const>, and <define> tag variables are scoped to their enclosing block. Hoisted references are readable only in code that runs after render: <script> bodies, <lifecycle> hooks, and event handlers. [!WARNING]
Attributes, <const>, and interpolations evaluate during render, before hoisted references are readable:

title: Repeated Tag Vars
content: When a hoisted tag variable originates inside a loop or repeated scope, it also implements the iterable protocol while calling it directly returns the first match:

title: Tag Parameters
content: A tag can pass values back into its content as |parameters| enclosed in pipes after the tag name: Renders: Parameters support full JavaScript function parameter syntax, including destructuring (<child|{ number }|>).

title: Tag Arguments
content: Pass positional arguments instead of named attributes with (...args) after the tag name: Custom tags accept either attributes or a single positional argument (with no body content). Dynamic tags and content bodies accept either attributes or multiple positional arguments (including spreads) alongside optional body content.

title: Tag Param Scope
content: Tag parameters are scoped strictly to the tag's content and are not accessible outside the body or inside attribute tags.

title: Doctype
content: A doctype writes directly to the HTML output in the template that renders the full document:

title: Comments
content:
Both HTML and JavaScript comments are supported and stripped from rendered output: [!NOTE]
To emit a literal HTML comment into the output, use <html-comment>.

title: Dynamic Tags
content: An ${expression} in the tag name position renders a native tag, custom tag, or tag content dynamically. Close dynamic tags with </> or self-close with />.

title: Dynamic Native Tags
content:
When the expression evaluates to a string, Marko renders a native HTML element with that tag name: [!CAUTION]
String tag names write directly into the document and expose the page to XSS if untrusted. Never pass user-provided strings as dynamic tag names.

title: Dynamic Custom Tags
content:
Pass an imported tag reference, <define> variable, or Marko.Body directly: Objects carrying a .content property (such as <define> tag variables) or a .default module export are unwrapped automatically. [!CAUTION]
Strings always render native HTML elements (document.createElement("my-tag-a")), never custom tags. Pass the imported tag reference instead:

title: Conditional Parent Tags
content: When a dynamic tag name evaluates to a falsy value, Marko renders its content without a wrapper element:

title: PascalCase Variables
content:
Any local variable starting with an uppercase letter (PascalCase) can be invoked directly as a tag without ${...}: [!WARNING]
A dot in a tag name is parsed as the class shorthand, so <Toolbar.Undo/> renders Toolbar with class="Undo". Use dynamic tag syntax to render a property on an object:

title: Custom Tag Discovery
content: Custom Tag Discovery Custom tags are reusable .marko components discovered automatically from the filesystem or installed packages without explicit imports.

title: Priority
content: Marko resolves a tag name in the following order: Local variables (PascalCase identifiers in scope) Core tags (built-in tags cannot be shadowed by custom tags) Relative custom tags in tags/ directories up to the nearest package.json Installed custom tags from dependencies in package.json Native HTML, SVG, and MathML tags

title: Local Variables
content:
When a tag name starts with an uppercase letter, Marko checks local scope first. This handles explicitly imported templates and <define> snippets: [!NOTE]
Reference a non-PascalCase local variable using dynamic tag syntax:

title: Relative Custom Tags
content:
For tags not matched in local scope, Marko walks upward from the current template's directory to the package root (package.json), checking each tags/ directory in precedence order: tags/TAG_NAME.marko tags/TAG_NAME/index.marko tags/TAG_NAME/TAG_NAME.marko One level deep inside a grouping folder pages/home/page.marko resolves: <app-header> <app-footer> <home-banner> pages/about/page.marko resolves: <app-header> <app-footer> <team-members> The home page cannot resolve <team-members> and the about page cannot resolve <home-banner>, scoping page-specific tags to their respective subtrees. [!NOTE]
Marko 5 discovered relative tags in components/ directories, which are now used as a heuristic for Marko 5 interop.

title: Grouping Folders
content: Related tags can be organized one level deep inside a folder that is not itself a tag. The folder name organizes files on disk without changing tag names: This discovers <menu-button>, <icon-chevron>, and <icon-plus>. Grouping rules: Grouping applies one level deep (tags/icons/outline/icon-star.marko is not discovered). A folder containing index.marko, a matching FOLDER_NAME.marko, or marko-tag.json is treated as a single tag rather than a grouping folder, so helper files alongside it are not crawled. tags, components, and node_modules folders are never treated as grouping folders. Dot-prefixed folders (such as .hidden) are skipped; non-leading dots (such as legacy.v1) still group.

title: Installed Custom Tags
content:
Marko inspects packages listed in package.json (dependencies, peerDependencies, and devDependencies) for a root marko.json with an "exports" directory: If the package defines a package.json "exports" map, it must also expose the directory named in marko.json because compiled consumer templates import discovered tags by their package path (such as @acme/ui/dist/tags/acme-icon/index.marko): TypeScript tag libraries publish .d.marko.ts declarations emitted by @marko/type-check alongside their templates (see TypeScript). [!TIP]
To keep internal helper tags private to a library, place them in a nested tags/ directory inside the exported directory (for example dist/tags/tags/). [!CAUTION]
When two packages export the same tag name, Marko selects the first one discovered. Prefix library tag names (for example ebay-) to avoid collisions, or import by path to disambiguate.

title: Native Tag Registration
content: The compiler recognizes standard HTML, SVG, and MathML tags. To emit non-standard elements or custom elements verbatim as native HTML tags, register them in a marko.json beside the template or in an ancestor directory:

title: Supporting Files
content: Marko automatically discovers adjacent stylesheets for any .marko template using a single extension (<name>.style.<ext>, or style.<ext> next to index.marko). A tag directory may also include a marko-tag.json: Any single preprocessor extension (.css, .scss, .less, etc.) is supported.

title: <if> / <else>
content:
Conditionally renders content or applies attribute tags. An <if> renders when its value= attribute (shorthand used below) is truthy. An <else> may include an if= condition to chain branches, evaluated in order: [!TIP]
<if> discards its DOM and state when hidden and rebuilds fresh state when shown again. To toggle visibility while preserving state, use <show>.

title: <show>
content:
Toggles whether its content is attached to the document based on whether value= is truthy: Unlike <if>, <show> renders its content once and keeps it mounted. Toggling value= only attaches or detaches the DOM nodes, preserving tag variables, form values, and DOM state: Because the content is built inline in the surrounding template, a reactive <show> ships only a small toggle helper rather than the template code to recreate its body. A statically truthy <show> compiles to plain markup with no runtime overhead. [!TIP]
Use <show> for content that toggles frequently, holds state worth preserving (form inputs, stateful components, or <lifecycle> widgets), or contains bulky static markup. Use <if> when hidden content should not render or appear in server HTML. [!NOTE]
Hidden content renders on the server inside a wrapper with the hidden attribute so it can resume without re-rendering; once toggled in the browser, hidden nodes are detached from the document. Because nodes leave the document, transient browser state such as focus and text selection resets on hide. <show> requires content and accepts only value=.

title: <for>
content: Iterates over collections or numeric ranges to render content or apply attribute tags, exposing iteration values via tag parameters: Arrays and iterables with of=: Object entries with in=: Exclusive numeric ranges with until=, from=, and step=: Inclusive numeric ranges with to=, from=, and step=: step= accepts negative or fractional values: A nullish of= or in= renders nothing, so optional values such as repeated attribute tags can be iterated directly. Pass by= on a content-rendering <for> to key each iteration so DOM nodes and local state persist across reorderings. by= accepts a function receiving the loop parameters, or a property name string when using of=: Each key must be a string or number unique within the loop.

title: <let>
content:
Declares mutable reactive state through its tag variable, initialized from value=: Reassigning count updates every expression that reads it. [!NOTE]
An uncontrolled <let> uses value= only as its initial value. Subsequent changes to the initializing expression do not overwrite the variable unless the <let> is controllable. Under TypeScript's strictNullChecks, a <let> initialized to null keeps the type null without widening; supply a type argument or assertion such as <let<string | null>/selected=null> or <let/selected=null as string | null>.

title: Controllable Let
content: Adding valueChange= makes <let> controllable, matching native tag change handlers. Writes to the tag variable invoke valueChange instead of mutating local state directly: In components, forwarding input.count via two-way binding (<let/count:=input.count>, shorthand for <let/count=input.count valueChange=input.countChange>) lets callers choose uncontrolled or controlled mode: To make count?: number optional with a default value, pass value= and valueChange= explicitly since := cannot take a fallback such as ?? 0:

title: <const>
content:
Declares a reactive derived value computed from value= and exposed through its tag variable: Because updates are batched, reassigning count updates doubleCount when the queue flushes rather than synchronously inside the handler (see Stale Derived Values). [!NOTE]
<const> is initialized per component instance. For module-wide constants shared across all instances, use static const. [!TIP]
<const> is conceptually equivalent to a component returning input.value:

title: <return>
content:
Exposes a tag variable from a custom tag via value=: [!WARNING]
Each template or tag content body may contain at most one <return> at its top level. Express conditional return values inside value= rather than placing <return> inside <if> or <for>.

title: Assignable Return Value
content: Provide valueChange= on <return> to allow callers to assign to the exposed tag variable:

title: Content Return
content: A tag content block may also contain <return>, read via a tag variable on the tag that renders that content. With <define>, a snippet can encapsulate state and expose it at its call site: For custom tags receiving input.content, pass the return type as the second type argument to Marko.Body:

title: <script>
content:
Runs reactive side effects in the browser after the DOM has mounted and updated, including child tag DOM. A <script> re-runs whenever any reactive tag variable, tag parameter, or input property read inside its body changes. Reading a DOM element getter (such as myButton()) or assigning to a <let> without reading it does not subscribe the effect. Pair <script> with $signal to clean up listeners, timers, or subscriptions before each re-run and on unmount: [!NOTE]
Execution order between separate <script> tags (and <lifecycle> hooks) is not guaranteed by source order. A <script> that reads a reactive tag variable attaches to that variable's initialization, so it can run before an earlier <script> that reads no reactive state. Additionally, reading a reactive variable anywhere inside <script> (including inside a registered event callback) subscribes the effect and aborts $signal on every change. For run-once setup that reads state in callbacks, or for paired restore-and-persist flows, use <lifecycle>.

title: Function Value
content: An effect can also be supplied via value= (written with =), receiving no arguments and re-running under the same rules:

title: Async Effects
content:
Using await in a <script> body compiles it to an async function that runs without blocking other effects: [!WARNING]
$signal resolves to the active run's signal, so capture it in a local variable before any await. [!TIP]
To emit a literal HTML <script> element instead of a Marko effect, use <html-script>.

title: <style>
content: Extracts and bundles CSS so each stylesheet loads once regardless of how many times a template renders: Append an extension to use a CSS preprocessor such as SCSS or Less: Adding a tag variable compiles <style> as a CSS Module, exposing scoped class names as an object:

title: Dynamic Values
content:
<style> accepts ${...} interpolations in CSS declaration value positions: The stylesheet remains static and extracted into the CSS bundle. Each interpolation compiles to a CSS custom property scoped via a small runtime <style> element to subsequent sibling elements and their descendants, updating only the custom property when state changes. Values are escaped so untrusted input cannot break out of the stylesheet. [!NOTE]
Place a <style> tag with dynamic values before the sibling elements it styles. Interpolations are valid in CSS declaration values (not selectors, at-rule preludes, property names, quoted strings, unquoted url(...), or concatenated directly with adjacent tokens like ${size}px or 10${x}). Include units in the value or multiply with calc(): [!TIP]
To emit a literal inline HTML <style> element, use <html-style>.

title: <define>
content:
Creates reusable local markup snippets within a template: The tag variable exposes all attributes passed to <define> (including its content). A <return> inside the body is exposed at the call site where the snippet renders (see Content Return). [!TIP]
<define> is conceptually equivalent to a component returning input:

title: <lifecycle>
content:
Synchronizes imperative browser APIs across mount, update, and destroy phases: Any reactive value read by the tag's attributes triggers onUpdate, including values read inside onMount, onDestroy, or callbacks they create. Before each onUpdate, tag attributes are reassigned onto this, keeping this consistent across the tag's lifetime so callbacks registered in onMount always read fresh values. This also fits restore-and-persist flows (restore once in onMount, persist changes in onUpdate). Returning an object from onMount attaches its properties to this with automatic type inference: [!WARNING]
Because tag attributes are reassigned onto this on every update, onMount must not return or assign property names that collide with attributes on the <lifecycle> tag. Extra properties can also be assigned directly onto this by supplying a type argument:

title: <id>
content: Exposes a short, unique ID string through its tag variable, suitable for HTML id and ARIA attributes: When value= is a non-empty string, <id> returns that value instead; undefined, null, false, and "" fall back to the generated ID:

title: <log>
content: Calls console.log with value= on initial render (server and client) and whenever any reactive value read in value= changes:

title: <debug>
content: Inserts a debugger statement that pauses when the tag renders: When given a value= attribute, <debug> runs on initial render and whenever any reactive dependency in value= changes:

title: <await>
content: Unwraps a promise from value= and passes its resolved value through a tag parameter. Non-promise values render synchronously without triggering a placeholder: When nested inside a <try> tag with @placeholder, the placeholder displays while the promise is pending:

title: <try>
content: Defines error and async boundaries around its content. Accepts @catch and @placeholder attribute tags; at least one must be provided.

title: @catch
content: Catches errors thrown while rendering the <try> content or its @placeholder, including rejected <await> promises and failed lazy-loaded tag fetches. The thrown error is passed as the @catch tag parameter: Errors thrown inside event handlers, <script> bodies, or <lifecycle> hooks occur outside the render path and propagate to the standard window error handler rather than @catch.

title: @placeholder
content: Displays fallback content while any nested <await> promise is pending, or while a lazily loaded tag is waiting for its trigger or loading its bundle in the browser.

title: <html-comment>
content: Outputs a literal HTML <!-- comment --> (standard comments are stripped). Interpolations inside <html-comment> escape > to >: Exposes a tag variable getter returning the DOM Comment node:

title: <html-script> & <html-style>
content:
Marko's <script> and <style> tags provide reactive browser effects and bundled CSS. When a literal HTML <script> or <style> element is required (such as an import map or inline JSON data), use <html-script> and <html-style>: [!CAUTION]
Contents of <html-script> and <html-style> execute as code, and interpolations escape only enough to avoid closing the element, so untrusted values expose the page to XSS. Never interpolate user-provided content into them. Inside <svg> or <math>, these tags parse as markup rather than raw text, so an interpolated < opens a real element. Never nest them in SVG or MathML with user-provided content.

title: Concise Syntax
content: Concise Syntax Marko's concise syntax omits angle brackets and closing tags, using indentation to express nesting. Every .marko file starts in concise mode. An HTML-mode tag switches to HTML mode for its own body, returning to concise mode once closed so both syntaxes can coexist in one file.

title: Attributes on multiple lines
content: Attributes can be comma-separated on a single line or split across lines with trailing commas: Indented lines beginning with a leading comma also attach attributes to the preceding tag, which is the conventional multiline style:

title: Text
content:
Two or more hyphens (--) followed by whitespace begin tag content. When text follows on the same line, the text ends at the newline: When -- is followed by a newline, the text block runs until a matching run of hyphens or the next dedent. HTML-mode tags can appear freely inside text blocks: [!TIP]
Use more than two hyphens when the text itself contains --; the closing delimiter must use the same number of hyphens as the opening one.

title: Root Level Text
content: Because templates begin in concise mode, bare root text is parsed as tags with attributes: Prefix root-level text with -- delimiters:

title: Compiler API
content: Compiler API @marko/compiler compiles .marko templates into JavaScript modules. Bundler integrations invoke it automatically; use this API directly when building bundler plugins, test transforms, or custom tooling.

title: Compile Functions
content: Each compile function provides an async form and a synchronous *Sync counterpart with identical arguments.

title: compile(src, filename, options)
content: Parameter Details src Template source string filename Template path used to resolve tags, relative imports, and its ID options Optional options overriding configured defaults Returns a Promise of the compile result; compileSync(src, filename, options) returns it synchronously. filename does not need to exist on disk.

title: compileFile(filename, options)
content: Reads filename via fileSystem and compiles it. compileFileSync(filename, options) is the synchronous form.

title: Compile Result
content: Property Details code Compiled JavaScript, or null when code is false map Source map when sourceMaps is true or "both" (and code is enabled without entry), else null ast Final Babel AST when ast is true, otherwise null meta Metadata gathered during compilation

title: Metadata
content: Property Details id Template ID shared between server and browser outputs watchFiles Non-template files affecting output (such as marko.json) for bundler file watching analyzedTags Optional list of templates whose analysis informed this compile and invalidate it on change diagnostics Errors, warnings, deprecations, and suggestions with type, label, loc, and optional fix api Component API ("tags" or "class"), or undefined for custom translators without preferAPI

title: Errors
content: Failed compiles throw a CompileError (check err.name === "CompileError" or "CompileErrors", as these classes are not exported). Its message includes the file location and code frame; integrations formatting their own diagnostics read: Property Details label Error text without location or code frame loc Optional source range (start, optional end lines and columns) frame Formatted code frame filename Template path Multiple errors throw a CompileErrors object with an errors array of CompileError instances.

title: Configuration
content: configure(options) replaces the default options for all subsequent compiles. Per-call options override defaults for that call only. Initial defaults can also be supplied as a JSON string in the MARKO_CONFIG environment variable.

title: Require Hook
content: @marko/compiler/register installs a Node.js CommonJS require hook for .marko files (always compiling with modules: "cjs"):

title: output
content: Value Output "html" Server output that renders HTML (default) "dom" Browser output that renders and updates the DOM "migrate" Template source after running migrations, without translating "source" Parsed template source, useful with ast Compiling the same template with "html" and "dom" produces its server and browser halves (see Targeted Compilation).

title: entry
content: Compiles the template as an entry point rather than a plain module. Requires linkAssets. Value Entry "page" With output: "html", wraps the page to write its asset tags. With output: "dom", emits the browser entry for that page "load" With output: "dom", emits the browser entry for a lazily loaded template

title: linkAssets
content: Connects server output to browser asset bundles. Pass the same linkAssets configuration to both server and browser compiles, and render pages through their entry: "page" module so asset tags flush into the HTML. Property Details onAsset onAsset(kind, file, id) called for each page ("page") or lazy import ("load") needing a matching output: "dom" entry runtime Absolute or virtual module ID imported by server output; exports flush($global, type, id) returning "block" or "defer" HTML tags

title: resolveVirtualDependency
content: Templates can emit auxiliary virtual modules for <style> blocks and browser registration helpers. The compiler calls resolveVirtualDependency(filename, dep) for each virtual module and imports the returned specifier: Parameter Details filename Template that produced the virtual module dep.virtualPath Suggested path (such as ./card.marko.css) dep.code Virtual module source dep.map Source map when sourceMaps is true or "both" Preserving virtualPath's extension lets the bundler apply standard CSS/JS handling. Without this option, <style> blocks are omitted from output; browser builds with cross-template registered imports require it.

title: modules
content: Output module format: "esm" (default) or "cjs".

title: optimize
content: Enables production output: imports the production runtime and shortens internal identifiers. Defaults to true when NODE_ENV is set to anything other than "development". MARKO_DEBUG overrides this, disabling optimization unless set to false or 0.

title: optimizeKnownTemplates
content: Ordered list of template paths assigned short sequential IDs when optimize is enabled. Server and browser builds must share the same list.

title: runtimeId
content: Isolates multiple Marko runtimes on one page. Must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.

title: sourceMaps
content: Value Output false No source map (default) true Source map in result map "inline" Source map comment inlined into code "both" Both map and inline comment

title: code
content: Defaults to true. Set to false to skip code generation when only meta or ast is needed.

title: ast
content: Defaults to false. Set to true to include the final Babel AST in the result.

title: stripTypes
content: Strips TypeScript syntax from output. Defaults to true for every output except "source" and "migrate".

title: translator
content: Translator module ID or object. Defaults to the installed marko package's translator (or a @marko/runtime-* dependency in package.json).

title: fileSystem
content: An fs-compatible object (readFileSync, statSync, readdirSync, plus readFile for compileFile, and optional realpathSync to resolve symlinked packages such as pnpm stores). Defaults to Node's fs.

title: cache
content: A Map caching analyzed templates across compiles until a template or dependency changes. Compiles sharing a cache must use identical options apart from output and entry ("source" and "migrate" bypass the cache). Defaults to a shared process-wide Map.

title: babelConfig
content: Babel options merged into the compiler's parse and generate configuration.

title: getTemplateId
content: A (filename) => id hook overriding the default top-level template ID (percent-encoded root-relative path, or short hash/sequential ID when optimize is enabled). Unsafe characters in the returned ID are percent-encoded.

title: errorRecovery
content: When true, records recoverable errors in meta.diagnostics instead of throwing (skipping translation and returning empty code when errors occur), useful for editor tooling.

title: applyFixes
content: A Map selecting which migration fixes apply by diagnostic index and passing each mapped value to its fix. Defaults to applying all fixes.

title: Tag Libraries
content: The taglib namespace controls tag discovery: Function Details register(id, props) Registers a tag library. Without props, loads a .json file path directly or <id>/marko.json for a package name excludeDir(dirname) Excludes dirname from tag discovery excludePackage(name) Excludes package name from tag discovery buildLookup(dirname, translator?, onError?, fileSystem?) Builds the tag lookup for dirname using configured defaults; onError handles failed tag libraries without throwing clearCaches() Clears cached tag libraries after editing marko.json, marko-tag.json, or package.json (also clear cache to recompile dependent templates)

title: Marko in September 2026
content: Marko in September 2026 [!TLDR] Unkeyed loops, dynamic tags, and lazily loaded pages ship less JavaScript The Prettier plugin no longer deletes code after a syntax error or drops comments More TypeScript syntax works directly in templates Clearer compile errors and a new Compiler API reference Persisted pages are close, built on a more rigorous compiler analysis that already benefits every app September shipped 25 releases across the compiler, runtime, editor tooling, and integrations. Pages got smaller, the formatter stopped losing code, more TypeScript works in templates, and compile errors got clearer. Persisted pages are nearly here, and the compiler analysis behind them has already landed for every app.

title: Smaller Bundles
content: Pages ship less without any template changes. A <for> without by= no longer ships the code for reordering keyed rows, saving about 190 to 240 bytes brotli on pages with only unkeyed loops (marko#4231), and a by= key is treated as constant within its row (marko#4254). A dynamic tag's body is bundled only when the browser can render it, so string tag names, names that resolve to known templates, and wrappers chosen only by input stay out of the client bundle (marko#4203, marko#4222, marko#4164). The same goes for static content passed to a local <define>, content passed only through a native spread, and attribute tags a child never reads (marko#4202, marko#4249, marko#4341). With lazy loading, a parent template that only revives through its lazily loaded child stays out of the eager bundle (marko#4314), and tags lazily loading the same template share one loader (marko#4269). Registrations, streamed resume data, and <try> renderers also got smaller (marko#4201, marko#4188, marko#4093).

title: Formatting
content: The Prettier plugin no longer changes what a template means. A template with a syntax error used to print only the part before the error, so prettier --write deleted the rest of the file; it now fails with a code frame and leaves the file alone (prettier#147). Comments inside an open tag are kept (prettier#154, prettier#153), backslashes in text no longer multiply on each run (prettier#151), spaces that render beside inline tags are preserved (prettier#156), and formatting without a JavaScript parser keeps async methods and scriptlet $ (prettier#150). In editors, Format Document works alongside other Prettier plugins such as Tailwind's (language-server#603), and quick fixes keep comments, types, and escapes (marko#4238, marko#4247, marko#4302).

title: Improvements
content: The rest of the month's feature work went into error messages and documentation.

title: Error Messages
content: Extra <for> parameters and a load import used before its import statement are now compile errors, and a string content on a native tag is a type error (marko#4179, marko#4279, marko#4304). <DIV> reports that tag names are case-sensitive (marko#4178), spreading arguments into a custom tag is caught at compile time (marko#4092), a root interface or enum gets the hint to use static (marko#4265), and <effect> with a body points at <script> (marko#4266). @marko/vite prints compile errors with their file:line:column and one code frame, naming the child template when the error is in one (vite#318, marko#4223). Long lines are trimmed in code frames, and parsing is linear in sibling count, so a template with 16,000 siblings parses in 0.35 seconds rather than 2.9 (marko#4300).

title: TypeScript Syntax
content: More TypeScript works directly in templates. A trailing non-null assertion ends an attribute value instead of swallowing the next attribute or the end of the tag, void ends a type annotation, and delete and ...new read as the JavaScript they are (htmljs-parser#253, htmljs-parser#254, htmljs-parser#255). Highlighting in VS Code, tree-sitter editors, and TextMate follows the same rules (language-server#608, tree-sitter#15, marko-tmbundle#21).

title: Documentation
content: A new Compiler API reference covers compiling templates and every compiler option (website#298), and let vs const is now a full article (website#289). The TypeScript guide recommends that tag libraries publish the .d.marko files @marko/type-check emits (website#294), and <html-script> and <html-style> now note that their interpolations run as code (website#299).

title: Docs Site
content: The playground can install component libraries through package.json (website#292), docs search finds the section for a bare symbol such as @ or ${ (website#295), and the mobile docs menu fits a whole section on one screen (website#239).

title: Native Tags
content: The native <search> element compiles and type-checks like any other HTML element (marko#3313).

title: Fixes
content: Fixes this month centered on streaming, resume, and less common template shapes. Interacting with a page while <await> content streams keeps the newest value, and @placeholder no longer flickers or stays up (marko#4258, marko#4264, marko#4272, marko#4349, marko#4350, marko#4359). Tag variables, controllable <let> handlers, spread attributes, and derived values stay correct after resume (marko#4347, marko#4317, marko#4270, marko#4197). Dynamic tags with nullable names or a choice between templates, and recursive <define> tags, render correctly (marko#4274, marko#4340, marko#4318, marko#4321). Attribute tags built with <if> and <for> keep every item and their loop values (marko#4232, marko#4256). load: "render" imports stay lazy, and a lazily loaded template with only styles links its stylesheet (marko#4279, vite#316). A marko@5 app that also lists @marko/runtime-tags keeps compiling its Class API templates (marko#4268). Full details for every change are in the release notes of each package on GitHub.

title: Coming Soon
content: Persisted pages, which keep a page alive across navigations by patching it in place, are very close. Every template now renders as patches, the server no longer resends shells the page already holds, and lazy templates, <try>, and streaming content patch the way they render in a document. The work also pushed the compiler's analysis to be exact about which values the server drives and which the browser owns. That rework has already landed on main for every app, and several of this month's fixes came out of it. Marko has also joined the Opus 5.5 video generation bandwagon with a persisted pages trailer.
